security_audit.summary: The external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code spans, and JavaScript template literals in D3 examples. The hardcoded URL is an HTTPS D3.js CDN example, not exfiltration. One semantic issue remains: the tooltip sample uses .html with data-derived content, which can teach unsafe DOM rendering.

remediation.issue: Tooltip example renders data with HTML.
remediation.suggestion: Use .text(...) for tooltip values, or sanitize trusted markup before rendering it with HTML APIs.

remediation.issue: CDN setup example does not mention integrity controls.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer package imports, or add Subresource Integrity and a pinned D3 version when showing CDN setup.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe HTML Tooltip Rendering Example
semantic_findings.description: The tooltip example writes a data-derived value with .html(...). If users adapt this pattern with untrusted data, HTML payloads could render in the page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 146 uses .html with an interpolated data value in a reusable D3 tooltip pattern. The example appears numeric, so exploitability depends on user data, but the pattern can teach unsafe rendering.

content.value_statement: Custom charts often need interactions that simple chart libraries cannot express. This skill guides D3.js SVG setup, data binding, scales, axes, tooltips, zoom, transitions, and color choices.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose D3.js instead of Three.js, Chart.js, or Recharts.
Shows setup with npm imports or D3 CDN script references.
Provides an SVG workflow for dimensions, margins, scales, axes, and data joins.
Gives examples for bar charts, line charts, and pie charts.
Covers tooltips, zoom and pan, transitions, scales, and color schemes.
Notes validation, responsiveness, performance, accessibility, and cleanup practices.
limitations: It does not include a complete application scaffold or build configuration.
It does not cover force layouts, maps, or brush interactions in detail.
It does not validate user datasets or guarantee chart accessibility automatically.
CDN examples require security hardening for production use.

use_cases.title: Prototype Custom Charts
use_cases.description: Create SVG chart structures with scales, axes, data joins, and visual marks for nonstandard data views.

use_cases.title: Prepare Analytical Graphics
use_cases.description: Turn tabular data into bar, line, or pie chart concepts with clear scale and color choices.

use_cases.title: Add Dashboard Interaction
use_cases.description: Enhance existing charts with hover details, zoom, pan, transitions, and redraw cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Use d3-viz to create a responsive bar chart for a dataset with category and value fields. Include axes, margins, labels, and cleanup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Chart Interactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use d3-viz to add tooltip and hover states to my existing SVG chart. Keep user data rendered as text, not raw HTML.

prompt_templates.title: Review a D3 Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use d3-viz to review my D3 chart structure for data binding, scales, cleanup, responsiveness, and accessibility. Suggest concise changes before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Complex Visualization
prompt_templates.prompt: Use d3-viz to plan a custom network or geographic visualization. Define data shape, SVG structure, interactions, transitions, performance constraints, and accessibility.

output_examples.input: A team needs a bar chart comparing monthly signups across categories.
output_examples.output: A D3 implementation plan with band and linear scales, margins, axes, rectangular marks, labels, and responsive sizing notes.

output_examples.input: A dashboard line chart needs hover details and smooth updates.
output_examples.output: Guidance for a line generator, time scale, tooltip behavior, transitions, cleanup steps, and safer text rendering.

output_examples.input: A dataset has many points and the SVG chart is slow.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to reduce DOM nodes, consider Canvas above large element counts, debounce resizing, and keep SVG for axes and labels.

best_practices: Validate null, NaN, and empty data before rendering.
Use ResizeObserver or container measurements for responsive charts.
Add ARIA labels, keyboard alternatives, and clear text labels where possible.
anti_patterns: Rendering untrusted data with .html in tooltips.
Redrawing without clearing old SVG elements.
Using D3 for simple charts when a smaller chart library is sufficient.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build custom D3.js charts, SVG visualizations, interactions, transitions, scales, and color schemes.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on D3 visualization patterns, not full project scaffolding or deployment setup.

faq.question: When should I choose D3.js?
faq.answer: Choose D3.js when you need custom SVG charts, advanced interactions, or visualizations beyond standard chart libraries.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: It reminds users to add ARIA labels and clear labels, but final accessibility review remains necessary.

faq.question: Is the CDN example production ready?
faq.answer: No. Production pages should prefer package imports or use pinned CDN scripts with integrity controls.
